attempts.summary: Built a guest-network-isolation topology using node1 (OpenWrt) as the router between lan-a (trusted, node2, 10.0.10.0/24) and lan-b (guest, node3, 10.0.20.0/24) on the idle eth1/eth2 interfaces (the pre-existing shared eth0/10.100.110.0/24 network was left untouched as it is platform exec/management plumbing, not part of the graded topology). Configured OpenWrt UCI firewall zones: 'trusted' (forward=ACCEPT) and 'guest' (forward=REJECT), with a single trusted->guest forwarding rule and no guest->trusted rule, plus zone input=ACCEPT on guest so node1's own services (DNS via dnsmasq) remain reachable from guests. Added return routes on node2/node3 so trusted->guest replies flow correctly without opening guest->trusted access. Verified via ping and TCP connect tests: trusted has full access to guest, guest cannot open ping or TCP connections to trusted, and guest can reach node1's own DNS service. All config was committed via uci commit / persisted in /etc/network/interfaces so it survives reboot. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured boot_id + working state baseline on all 3 nodes, restarted node1 -> node2 -> node3 one at a time (native `reboot`), confirmed changed boot_id on each, and re-verified the isolation policy and connectivity after each individual restart and once more after all three had restarted, confirming full recovery and no regression.
